findings.description: tsconfig.app.json changes `"strict": true` to `"strict": false`. Verified: at head, `tsc -b --noEmit` (validate:types, and the `tsc -b` step of `npm run build` in the CI Build job) exits 2 with 242 errors. For example, TanStack Router's `createRouter` argument now resolves to the type "strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json". With `strict: true` the same check exits 0, and the new files type-check cleanly. Typed ESLint also degrades: `npm run lint` reports `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment` errors on `useWatch(...)` in every trigger-fields file, including the unchanged flow-run-state file. Those errors disappear under strict. This also violates AGENTS.md rule 11. Fix: restore `"strict": true`.
findings.failureMode: `npm run build` / `npm run validate:types` fail (242 TS errors, exit 2) so the UI cannot build and CI type-check fails; strict type enforcement is removed repo-wide.
findings.title: strict:false breaks tsc build and disables strict checks

findings.description: The Status FormField's `name` switches between `trigger.expect` and `trigger.after` with posture. react-hook-form 7.69 `useController` calls `control.unregister(previousName)` when the name changes, so the chosen status is deleted. Verified: select "Not Ready" (expect=[prefect.deployment.not-ready]), switch to "Stays in", and both expect and after are undefined and the select shows "Select status"; switching back does not restore it. Both fields are optional in the schema, so the step still validates and the trigger is saved with no status filter. With Reactive, `expect` empty plus `match prefect.deployment.*` fires on every deployment event. The work-pool and work-queue templates keep a fixed binding and don't lose the selection. Fix: stop switching the FormField `name`. Hold the selected status in one stable binding and write `trigger.after`/`trigger.expect` explicitly for the current posture, moving the value when posture changes.
findings.failureMode: Choosing a status and then changing posture silently clears the status. The automation then has no deployment-status filter and fires on unrelated deployment events.
findings.title: Posture toggle wipes selected deployment status

findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` never returns an empty array (`"".split("\n")` is `[""]`), so the `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` fallback is dead and blank lines are stored. Verified: clearing the textarea sets `trigger.expect` to `[""]`, and typing a⏎⏎b⏎ gives `["a","","b",""]`. The server's `expects()` uses `matches("", event)`, which reduces to `event == ""`, so `expect: [""]` matches no event, whereas empty/undefined `expect` means "match any event". Fix: keep the raw textarea text in local state for display, and store only the non-blank lines in `trigger.expect` (undefined when there are none). That way Enter still inserts newlines.
findings.failureMode: A user who clears the Expected Events box (intending "any event") produces `expect: [""]`, a custom trigger that can never fire; blank lines add bogus "" event names.
findings.title: Custom events keep blank lines; cleared textarea stores [""]

findings.description: Threshold onChange is `field.onChange(parseInt(e.target.value))`, while every sibling template (deployment, work-queue, custom, flow-run-state) uses `Number(...)`. (1) biome.json sets `style/useNumberNamespace: "error"`; `biome ci` (run by the ui-v2-checks Lint job) exits 1 with this line as the only error. (2) Clearing the input stores NaN: React logs "Received NaN for the `value` attribute" and validation shows "Expected number, received nan" instead of the min(1) message the other templates show. Fix: use `Number(e.target.value)` like the siblings.
findings.failureMode: CI Lint job (`biome ci`) fails; clearing Threshold in the work-pool template puts NaN into form state with a misleading validation error.
findings.title: Work-pool threshold uses bare parseInt (fails biome ci; NaN on clear)

findings.description: The Status select always writes to `trigger.expect`, even when posture is Proactive ("Stays in"). Verified output for "Stays in" + "Not Ready": `{posture:"Proactive",within:30,expect:["prefect.work-pool.not-ready"]}`. Server Proactive triggers fire on the *absence* of `expect` events (`meets_threshold`: Proactive and count < threshold), so this fires in each window with no not-ready event, i.e. while the pool is healthy or recovered. That is the opposite of "stays in Not Ready". The repo's existing "Stays in" mapping (flow-run-state) and the deployment template in this PR put the state in `after`. The same defect is at work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36. Fix: when posture is Proactive, write the selected status to `trigger.after` (with the other statuses in `expect`); keep `expect` for Reactive.
findings.failureMode: A "work pool/queue stays Not Ready for N s" automation built by the wizard alerts when the pool/queue is NOT going not-ready, not when it stays not-ready.
findings.title: "Stays in" work pool/queue status stored in expect (inverted proactive trigger)

findings.description: Base read `config.get("identifier")`; head reads `config.get("bundle")`. In Tauri v2 `identifier` is a required top-level string and `bundle` is an object (`pub bundle: BundleConfig`), so `.as_str()` always yields None and `original_identifier` is None for every valid config (reproduced: head None vs base Some("com.tauri.dev")). `write_options`, called by `tauri android dev/build` and `tauri ios dev/build`, does `config.original_identifier().context("app configuration is missing an identifier")?`, so every mobile dev/build command aborts; `read_options` in the Xcode/Android Studio scripts hits the same error and panics via `.expect("failed to read CLI options")`. Fix: restore `config.get("identifier")`.
findings.failureMode: Any valid tauri.conf.json (e.g. `"identifier": "com.tauri.dev", "bundle": {...}`) → original_identifier None → `tauri android dev` / `tauri ios build` etc. fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier".
findings.title: original_identifier reads `bundle` object instead of top-level `identifier`

findings.description: Base: `extension() == Some("json") || extension() == Some("json5")`. Head: `... && ...`. A path can't have both extensions, so the condition is always false (reproduced for `tauri.conf.json`: head=false, base=true). `config_schema_validator()` is never called, no schema errors get logged, and the `exit(1)` for invalid configs never fires. Constraints that only the schema enforces are now accepted silently. For example, the `productName` regex is a schemars-only `validate(regex)` attribute, and serde ignores it: `"productName": "my/app"` gives the schema error `"my/app" does not match ...` at `/productName`, but the head never reports it. Fix: restore `||`.
findings.failureMode: tauri.conf.json with `"productName": "my/app"` (or any schema violation) → no validation errors, CLI continues instead of exiting 1.
findings.title: `||` changed to `&&` makes schema validation unreachable

findings.description: Base ended with `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;`. Head replaces it with `config_metadata.extensions.insert(MERGE_CONFIG_EXTENSION_NAME.into(), merge_config);`. The merged `value` is now computed and thrown away, so `inner` is never updated. That contradicts the function's doc, "merges the loaded config with the given value", and leaves `extensions` saying `--config` applies when `inner` doesn't include it. Impact is limited today: the only callers (android_studio_script.rs:98, xcode_script.rs:145) already call `reload` with the same configs, which masks the problem. Any path that relies on merge_with gets a stale config. Fix: restore the `inner` assignment.
findings.failureMode: merge_with(&[json!({"build":{"devUrl":"http://x"}})]) after get() → config.build.dev_url unchanged.
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies merged config to `inner`

findings.description: The `let schema: JsonValue = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(...)).expect(...)` line is ~150 chars, over rustfmt.toml `max_width = 100`. rustfmt wants `.expect(...)` on its own continuation line, so the mandated `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (AGENTS.md rule 3) fails. Fix: run cargo fmt (break before `.expect`).
findings.failureMode: CI format check job exits non-zero on this file.
findings.title: Line exceeds max_width; `cargo fmt --check` fails

findings.description: `config_metadata.extensions.insert(MERGE_CONFIG_EXTENSION_NAME.into(), merge_config);` exceeds the default chain_width (use_small_heuristics = "Default"); rustfmt reflows it into a vertical chain, so `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (AGENTS.md rule 3) fails on this line.
findings.failureMode: CI format check job exits non-zero on this file.
findings.title: Unformatted method chain; `cargo fmt --check` fails

findings.description: The atoms noRestrictedImports group changed from `@calcom/trpc/react` to `@calcom/trpc` + `@calcom/trpc/**` at level "error", but two atoms files the PR leaves untouched still import `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell` (ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx:12, SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx:6). With the same biome-staged.json the pre-commit hook uses, these files go from 0 errors at base to 2 `lint/style/noRestrictedImports` errors at head, so `biome lint` on atoms exits 1. The lint-staged hook now blocks any commit that touches these files, even with the SKIP_WARNINGS waiver. Fix: move QueryCell out of @calcom/trpc (e.g. an atoms-local copy) in this PR.
findings.failureMode: Staging SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx or ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx runs `biome lint --config-path=biome-staged.json`, which now reports 'atoms package should not import from @calcom/trpc.' as an error and aborts the commit (also with SKIP_WARNINGS=1). Any `biome lint` over packages/platform/atoms also exits 1.
findings.title: Broadened trpc ban makes existing atoms QueryCell imports lint errors

findings.description: The replacement `SlotInfo` declares `fromUser.id: string`, but the source type it replaces (`IGetAvailableSlots` → `IFromUser.id: number`) and the /slots/available payload use a numeric user id. `EventTypeCalendarViewComponent.tsx:115` passes `useAvailableSlots().data` to `useAvailableTimeSlots({ schedule?: IGetAvailableSlots })`, which now fails with TS2322 ('string' is not assignable to 'number'). The base type came from `Promise<IGetAvailableSlots>`, so this error is new. The publicly exported `useAvailableSlots` hook also ships the wrong id type. Fix: declare `id: number`.
findings.failureMode: tsc on atoms: EventTypeCalendarViewComponent.tsx:115 errors TS2322 (fromUser.id string vs number). Consumers of the exported useAvailableSlots who call without timeZone get raw OOO slots with numeric fromUser.id typed as string, so string ops or string-id comparisons compile but fail at runtime.
findings.title: Local SlotInfo types fromUser.id as string; server sends number

findings.description: `GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn` declares `days: string[]`, but the /atoms/schedules/all endpoint returns `getAvailabilityListHandler` output, where `Availability.days` is Prisma `Int[]` (number[]). The only consumer, `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper.tsx:84`, calls `getScheduleListItemData(schedule)`, whose parameter requires `days: number[]`. That call now fails with TS2345 ('string[]' is not assignable to 'number[]'). The base type was inferred from the handler and compiled. Fix: `days: number[]`.
findings.failureMode: tsc on atoms: ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper.tsx:84 errors TS2345 (days string[] vs number[]). The declared type also misstates the numeric weekday values the API returns.
findings.title: availability.days typed string[] but Prisma/API return number[]

findings.description: The PR moves `Slot` out of trpc, but the copy changes `userIds?: number[]` (deleted in trpc slots/types.ts: `userIds?: number[];`) to `userIds?: string[]`. Every other slot type in the repo, and the server's passthrough `userIds`, use numeric user ids. `Slot` is the payload type of the public `onTimeslotsLoaded` Booker prop, so consumers who typed their callback against the old `number[]` contract now get a contravariance compile error. Code relying on the new type compares string ids against numeric values. Fix: `userIds?: number[]`.
findings.failureMode: A platform consumer writes `onTimeslotsLoaded={(s: Record<string, {time: string; userIds?: number[]}[]>) => ...}` (the previous published shape), and it no longer compiles. Consumers following the new type treat numeric ids as strings.
findings.title: Moved Slot type silently changes userIds from number[] to string[]

findings.description: The new exported `validateCreateScheduleInput` throws plain `new Error('Invalid input: must be an object')` (line 40) and `new Error('Invalid input: name must be a non-empty string')` (line 46). Mandatory rule 10 forbids throwing generic Error objects without a typed code or statusCode. A validation failure from this helper therefore can't be told apart from other failures or mapped to a 400. Fix: throw a typed error (e.g. ErrorWithCode with a bad-request code) at both sites.
findings.failureMode: validateCreateScheduleInput({}) throws an uncategorized Error with no code or statusCode. That violates the mandate and leaves callers unable to classify it as a client-input error.
findings.title: New validator throws generic Error (AGENTS.md rule 10)

findings.description: Lines 39, 40, 45 and 46 use single-quoted string literals ('object', 'string', and both error messages). The repository's Biome config sets `quoteStyle: "double"`, which AGENTS.md rule 3 requires. `biome format` reports this file as unformatted and would rewrite all four lines. Fix: use double quotes (run `biome format --write`).
findings.failureMode: `npx biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits 1 with 'Formatter would have printed the following content' for lines 39/40/45/46.
findings.title: Single-quoted strings violate Biome formatting mandate

findings.description: XCTest only discovers methods prefixed with `test`. After the rename to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`, TestRail case 2864380 never runs, and nothing records it as skipped. FullFunctionalTestPlan runs all of ShareLongPressTests (the class is not skipped there) and used to execute this test. This breaks AGENTS.md rule 6 (test methods start with 'test'). AccessibilityTestPlan still lists `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`. Fix: restore the `test` prefix; if the case must be disabled, do it visibly with `throw XCTSkip(...)` or a plan skip entry.
findings.failureMode: FullFunctionalTestPlan run: the bookmark→Reminders share test is no longer discovered, so a regression in that flow goes unreported. The suite passes without running it or marking it skipped.
findings.title: Rename to verify… silently removes test from every run

findings.description: The condition skips the Light-theme reset for every OnboardingTests test on iPad, not just the skipped testSelectBottomPlacement. testFirstRunTourDarkMode has no iPad guard, runs on iPad in FullFunctionalTestPlan, and calls switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Dark"). The app's DefaultThemeManager keeps the theme in UserDefaults.standard, which ClearProfile/resetApplication does not clear (DisplaySettingTests needs removeApp() to get defaults). On iPad the Dark theme therefore persists into every later test. The comment on line 30 ("the theme is not changed there") is wrong. Fix: remove the `|| iPad()` clause so the reset is skipped only for testSelectBottomPlacement.
findings.failureMode: iPad, iOS 17+: testFirstRunTourDarkMode switches to Dark; tearDown hits `iPad()` and skips the reset. Later tests in the run (other OnboardingTests and later classes) launch with a persisted Dark theme instead of Light, which breaks test isolation.
findings.title: `|| iPad()` disables theme reset on iPad; Dark theme from testFirstRunTourDarkMode leaks

findings.description: The bookmark long press dropped from 1.0s to 0.5s. BookmarksViewController's UILongPressGestureRecognizer uses the default minimumPressDuration of 0.5s, so each synthesized press lifts at the moment .began would fire. Every retry in pressWithRetry uses the same borderline duration. The same panel is pressed for 1.5s in BookmarksTests.longPressBookmarkCell, and no other test in the repo long-presses for under 1s. Fix: use a duration well above the threshold (1.5s, as in BookmarksTests).
findings.failureMode: In testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteSendLinkDevice or CopyURL, touch-up can be processed before the recognizer reaches .began, so the context menu never opens. If all attempts race the same way, pressWithRetry XCTFails. This makes flakiness worse, which is the opposite of the fix's aim.
findings.title: Long-press shortened to 0.5s, exactly the recognizer threshold

findings.description: On iOS 17+, when the test is testSelectBottomPlacement or runs on iPad, the new `return` exits tearDown before `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()`. BaseTestCase.tearDown (app.terminate + XCTestCase.tearDown) is bypassed, so the app is left running and the teardown chain is broken for every OnboardingTests test on iPad. Compare C_AddressesTests.tearDown, which skips the theme reset conditionally and still terminates and calls super. Fix: drop the `return` and guard only the switchThemeToDarkOrLight call, so terminate/super always run.
findings.failureMode: iPad iOS 17+ run of any OnboardingTests test (or iPhone testSelectBottomPlacement): tearDown returns at line 31, so app.terminate()/super.tearDown() never execute; the app stays alive after the test and base-class cleanup is bypassed.
findings.title: Early return in tearDown skips app.terminate() and super.tearDown()

findings.description: `for (int j = 0; j <= keys_result->numkeys; j++)` iterates one past the last key. At j==numkeys it reads keys_result->keys[numkeys] (zeroed keysbuf slot -> pos 0 -> argv[0], the command name; when numkeys exactly fills keysbuf, the bytes of the `keys` pointer -> garbage argv index) and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] past the malloc'd buffer. Result in cluster mode: nearly every keyed command (SET/GET/INCR foo) is rejected with CROSSSLOT because the command name hashes to another slot. A 6-key same-slot command (MGET {t}1..{t}6) crashes the server inside preprocessCommand, which runs before AUTH, so an unauthenticated client can take the node down. getSlotFromCommand (db.c:438) goes through the same loop, so asmFeedMigrationClient sets cross_slot_during_propagating and cancels slot migrations, and asmModulePropagateBeforeSlotSnapshot returns ENOTSUP. Fix: `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Cluster node: `SET foo bar` -> CROSSSLOT error. Unauthenticated `MGET {t}1 {t}2 {t}3 {t}4 {t}5 {t}6` -> server crashes with SIGSEGV/SIGBUS in extractSlotFromKeysResult (reproduced on the built head).
findings.title: Off-by-one loop bound reads/writes past keys and slot_buffer

findings.description: New `malloc` (line 1110) and `free` (lines 1120, 1124) in extractSlotFromKeysResult. server.h marks malloc/free `__attribute__((deprecated))` under __GNUC__ and src/Makefile's default WARN has `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`, so `make` fails compiling cluster.o ("'malloc' is deprecated"). Also violates AGENTS.md rule 2 (zmalloc/zfree only) and rule 4 (-Werror build). Even if forced to compile, allocation is untracked by used_memory and unchecked for NULL, on the per-command hot path. Fix: use zmalloc/zfree (or drop the never-read slot_buffer).
findings.failureMode: Default `make` in src/ fails: cluster.c:1110:24: error: 'malloc' is deprecated [-Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations] (plus two 'free' errors) -> redis-server cannot be built.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free breaks default build and zmalloc mandate

findings.description: Base pinned `toolbar.leadingAnchor` to `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor` (== container leading). The diff changes it to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. Since rightSkeleton.leading == container.trailing and its width == container.width - 32, toolbar.leading becomes container.trailing + width - 32 while toolbar.trailing == container.trailing, i.e. a negative-width toolbar placed off-screen. swiping_tabs defaults to true on non-iPad, so on iPhone the main address bar is laid out wrong/invisible. Fix: restore `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`.
findings.failureMode: iPhone with default swiping_tabs=true: address toolbar gets width 32 - containerWidth and sits past the right edge; URL bar not usable.
findings.title: Toolbar leading pinned to right skeleton bar's trailing edge

findings.description: The rename replaced `pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` with `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews` (duplicate) instead of `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`. `updateActionStack` sets `button.alpha = 0` for every button newly added to a stack, and only `updateToolbarLayout` restores alpha to 1. Trailing page actions (reader mode, reload, stop loading, summarizer) are no longer in `stacks`, so they remain at alpha 0 permanently: invisible and not hit-testable. Fix: use `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` on line 332.
findings.failureMode: Load any page: reload/stop/reader-mode buttons are added to trailingPageActionStack with alpha 0 and never faded back in; they are invisible and untappable.
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons never restored to alpha 1

findings.description: A PR described as "removed unused code" adds `let isLandscape = UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation.isLandscape`, which is never read. It adds two new compiler warnings to the Client target: the value is never used, and `statusBarOrientation` has been deprecated since iOS 13. This is the only `statusBarOrientation` use in the repo. It also calls the concrete `UIApplication.shared` singleton directly, which violates AGENTS.md rule 8 (use protocol abstractions). Fix: delete this line and the comment above it.
findings.failureMode: Every build of AddressToolbarContainer emits unused-variable and iOS 13 deprecation warnings; new direct UIApplication.shared dependency breaks mandate 8.
findings.title: Dead isLandscape local uses deprecated UIApplication.shared API

findings.description: Base: `let hasPageActions = !pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty` (the trailing stack). The rename changed it to `leadingPageActionStack`. `locationDividerView` sits between `locationView` and `trailingPageActionStack`, so its width must track the trailing stack. With a `.default()` UX config (divider 4pt, public ToolbarKit API used by SampleBrowser), trailing-only actions (e.g. reload/stop) lose the divider, and leading-only actions (share) get a stray divider. Firefox uses `.experiment` (0pt), so current impact is limited. Fix: check `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`.
findings.failureMode: ToolbarKit consumer with .default() config and only trailing page actions: divider width 0 instead of 4; with only leading actions: 4pt divider next to empty trailing stack.
findings.title: Divider width now keyed off leading page actions

findings.description: The deleted line `toolbar.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor)` became `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. The next line keeps `toolbar.trailing == rightSkeletonAddressBar.leading`, and the skeleton is pinned with `rightSkeleton.leading == container.trailing` and `width == container.width - 32`. Together these force the toolbar to width `32 - containerWidth`, which is negative, and push its leading edge off-screen to the right. That conflicts with the toolbar's required internal constraints, so Auto Layout breaks a constraint and the main address bar is mispositioned or off-screen. Fix: restore `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`.
findings.failureMode: On any iPhone with the default `swiping_tabs: true` Nimbus value, `setupToolbarConstraints` installs contradictory required constraints. The address toolbar then lays out off-screen or collapsed instead of filling the container, and Auto Layout logs "Unable to simultaneously satisfy constraints".
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchored to right skeleton's trailing edge

findings.description: In the rename, the deleted line `pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` in `updateToolbarLayout` was replaced with `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews` (browser actions now appear twice) instead of `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`. `updateActionStack` sets `button.alpha = 0` on every button newly added to a stack (line 371), and the only ToolbarKit code that sets it back to 1.0 is the `stacks.forEach` at lines 341/346. Trailing page action buttons (reader mode, summarizer, reload, stop loading) are no longer in `stacks`. So they stay at alpha 0, which makes them invisible, and because their alpha is below 0.01 UIKit hit-testing skips them. Fix: use `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` on line 332.
findings.failureMode: Load any web page in the Firefox client: the trailing stack receives a reload/stop (and reader-mode/summarizer) button with alpha 0 that is never restored, so those address-bar buttons are invisible and cannot be tapped.
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons never faded back in (alpha stays 0)

findings.description: The deleted line `let hasPageActions = !pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty` (trailing stack) became `!leadingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty`. `locationDividerView` sits between `locationView` and `trailingPageActionStack` (line 272) and has a visible `layer1` background. So its width should depend on the trailing stack, not the leading one. Fix: use `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty`.
findings.failureMode: With the public `.default()` UX config (4pt divider): trailing-only page actions such as reload lose their divider, and leading-only actions such as share produce a stray divider next to an empty trailing stack. The Firefox client uses `.experiment` (0pt), so the in-repo visual impact is limited.
findings.title: Divider width now keyed on leading instead of trailing page actions

findings.description: This PR says it removes unused code, but it adds `let isLandscape = UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation.isLandscape` to `setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout`. Nothing reads the value, and the comment above it claims "layout adjustments" that do not exist. It reads the deprecated (iOS 13) `statusBarOrientation` API directly from `UIApplication.shared` instead of the repo's `UIWindow.isLandscape` helper or an injected application abstraction (AGENTS.md rule 8). The Client target gets two new compiler warnings (unused immutable value and deprecated API) and a misleading comment. Fix: delete lines 464-465.
findings.failureMode: Each AddressToolbarContainer init on iPhone evaluates a deprecated global API and discards the result. The build emits unused-variable and deprecation warnings, and the comment claims layout adjustments the code never makes.
findings.title: Unused isLandscape reads deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: The diff deletes `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and hardcodes `40` in both the height and width constraints of closeButton. AGENTS.md Rule 13 requires UI measurements to live in a nested UX struct; the removal was not needed for Swift 6 (a nested UX struct in a Toast subclass typechecks cleanly in Swift 6 mode). Fix: restore `private struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and use `UX.buttonSize` at both sites.
findings.failureMode: Mandated compliance rule (AGENTS.md #13) violated on changed lines; the square button size is now two independent literals that can drift apart on future edits.
findings.title: Close-button size moved out of UX struct into duplicated magic literals

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj) passes 7 objects but argc=6. The va_arg loop reads only 6, so newobj (the incremented value) is dropped. HINCRBYFLOAT is propagated as `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`, which hsetexParseArgs rejects as an arity error. With the default config, replicas and AOF replay skip the write: after DEBUG LOADAOF, HGET returns 10 instead of 12.5. With propagation-error-behavior panic or panic-on-replicas, the replica or AOF load panics. The suite's default.conf sets `panic`, so the existing info-keysizes replica test crashes the replica. Fix: pass 7.
findings.failureMode: Master runs HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1 → replica/AOF receive `HSETEX h KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f` → the replica logs an error and skips the command, and AOF replay does the same. Replicas diverge and the write is lost after an AOF restart. With propagation-error-behavior=panic, the replica or AOF load panics. The new test's stream pattern `{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}` also fails.
findings.title: HSETEX rewrite uses argc 6 for 7 args, dropping the value

findings.description: The base passed HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL; the diff drops HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. On both the LISTPACK_EX and HT paths, hashTypeSet then persists the existing field, so HINCRBYFLOAT on the master wipes the field TTL. The HSETEX KEEPTTL sent to replicas keeps it there, so the two diverge. Confirmed: HPTTL returns -1 on the master after HINCRBYFLOAT, and the existing test 'HINCRBYFLOAT - preserve expiration time of the field' fails for both encodings. Fix: restore `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`.

findings.description: `rendered = result.get("result")` is guarded only by `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)`, so None gets past the check and `return rendered` returns None from a method declared `-> str`. (1) CI's Python Style job runs basedpyright (strict) and mypy. Both fail on line 40: basedpyright reports `Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str"` and mypy reports `[return-value]`. (2) At runtime, an injected or subclassed executor (for example via the new DifyNodeFactory code_executor -> renderer wiring) whose result lacks `result` or has it set to None makes render_template return None. `_run` then evaluates `len(rendered)` and raises `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`, which escapes `except TemplateRenderError`. The node then fails as a generic WorkflowNodeError without inputs instead of a clean FAILED result. Fix: `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError("Template render result must be a string.")`.
findings.failureMode: An executor returns {} or {"result": None}, so render_template returns None and `len(None)` raises TypeError that escapes the TemplateRenderError handler. Separately, basedpyright and mypy fail the CI style job with a reportReturnType/return-value error on line 40.
findings.title: render_template can return None despite `-> str`; type checks fail and None crashes `len()`

Fix: move them into a collected `test_*.py` module that imports `core.workflow.entities.GraphInitParams` and `core.workflow.runtime.GraphRuntimeState`, and drop `graph=`.

findings.description: The new clause `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'` turns BUILD002 on only for the X.Y.1 patch. That is exactly the patch where the baseline is still stale: Baseline.Designer.props is still at 9.0.0, which is why this diff sets ValidateBaseline=false. With PatchVersion=1 and servicing on, the net10.0 builds pick up the 9.0 baseline items. Two packages hit this: Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client.Core has a baseline System.Threading.Channels reference, but the csproj only references it for non-.NETCoreApp targets. Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.Client has the same problem with System.Net.ServerSentEvents. In both cases UnusedBaselinePackageReference is non-empty, BUILD002 fires, and restore/build fails. For patches 2 and later the check never runs, so the servicing guard against dropped dependencies is silently disabled. Fix: use `!= '1'`.

findings.title: BUILD002 patch-version guard is inverted (== '1' instead of != '1')

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>. All five callers use `?` inside prepare_tools, which returns crate::Result: line 232 (AppRun), 239 (linuxdeploy), 245 (gtk), 251 (gstreamer), 259 (appimage plugin). crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError>, so each call site fails with E0277 and tauri-bundler does not compile on Linux. Reproduced with the exact lines: 5x E0277. Fix: restore a return type crate::Error can convert from, e.g. std::io::Result<()> as in the base.

findings.description: The base ran `fs::write(path, data)?;` and then `fs::set_permissions(...)`. The diff swaps the order. Every caller guarded by `!x.exists()` (AppRun, linuxdeploy, gstreamer plugin, appimage plugin) passes a path that does not exist yet, so set_permissions fails with ENOENT before anything is written. On a fresh tools cache, prepare_tools returns 'Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory', and the optional appimage-plugin download becomes a hard error too. Fix: write first, then set permissions.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling fails on any machine or CI runner without a pre-populated tauri tools cache.
findings.title: chmod now runs before the file is created

findings.description: The base condition `if !gtk.exists()` became `if gtk.exists()`. If the cache has no linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh, the inlined script is never written. linuxdeploy is always run with `--plugin gtk` (line ~199), so it cannot find the plugin and fails. Existing copies get rewritten on every run instead. Fix: restore `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: On clean caches (new users, CI runners), linuxdeploy fails because the gtk plugin is missing, so no AppImage is produced.
findings.title: Inverted check: gtk plugin only written when it already exists

findings.title: FileWriteError hand-implements Display/Error instead of thiserror

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC.handleDisplayActions routes `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()` (creates a reading-list record + toast) instead of `toggleReaderMode()`. After this change nothing in the reducer emits `.readerMode`, so every `showReaderMode` dispatch — toolbar reader-mode tap, summarizer-button long press, and VoiceOver magic tap (accessibilityPerformMagicTap) — never enables/disables reader mode and instead saves the page to the reading list. Fix: restore `displayView: .readerMode`.

findings.description: Condition changed from `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. isReaderModeURL requires scheme http, so the new expression equals isWebPage(): reader-mode URLs (http://localhost:PORT/reader-mode/page?url=...) are now forwarded in the cancelEdit ToolbarAction instead of nil. AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction uses `toolbarAction.url ?? state.url`, so the decoded displayURL that BVC set via urlDidChange is overwritten with the internal localhost URL; LocationView then renders its host ("localhost") and shows the raw URL on next edit. Fix: restore `currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: User is in reader mode, taps the tabs or menu toolbar button (or cancel while editing) → cancelEditMode dispatches cancelEdit with the raw localhost reader-mode URL → address bar shows/uses http://localhost:…/reader-mode/page?url=… instead of the original page URL.

Also breaks the existing unit test testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes: with default nil readerModeState the head yields isEnabled=true, which (via the pre-existing swapped extra args in ToolbarTelemetry) lands in savedExtras.isPrivate and fails `XCTAssertEqual(savedExtras.isPrivate, false)`. Fix: restore `.available: true` / `default: false`.
findings.failureMode: Every reader-mode button tap records the inverted open/close value in toolbar.reader_mode_button_tapped; ToolbarMiddlewareTests reader-mode tap test fails in CI.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap telemetry `enabled` value inverted

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, but every caller in prepare_tools (lines 232, 239, 245, 251, 259) uses `?` inside a fn returning crate::Result. crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> (only #[from] io::Error, anyhow::Error, ...), so rustc emits E0277 "`?` couldn't convert the error to `Error`". The appimage module is compiled only on Linux, so tauri-bundler (and tauri-cli) fail to build on Linux and the ubuntu clippy CI job fails. Fix: make write_and_make_executable return crate::Result<()> (e.g. map io errors via the existing fs_context) so `?` converts.

findings.description: Base order was `fs::write(path, data)?;` then `fs::set_permissions(...)`. The diff swaps them, so on a fresh tools cache (first AppImage build, clean CI runner) chmod targets a file that does not exist yet and returns NotFound before anything is written. prepare_tools propagates it at the first write (AppRun), so AppImage bundling aborts with "Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory". A successful download of the optional appimage plugin also becomes fatal. Fix: call fs::write first, then fs::set_permissions.

findings.title: set_permissions now runs before write; fails with ENOENT for new tool files

The new `if gtk.exists()` means that on a fresh tools directory linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never written. linuxdeploy is always run with `--plugin gtk`, so it cannot find the plugin and AppImage bundling fails for every new user or clean CI runner. Fix: restore `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: On a clean cache, linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is missing; linuxdeploy --plugin gtk fails (plugin not found) and no AppImage is produced.
findings.title: Inverted guard: gtk plugin written only if it already exists

findings.description: The new set_permissions line is 101 chars, over rustfmt.toml max_width = 100. rustfmt --check reports a diff (it wants `.map_err(FileWriteError::Permissions)?;` on its own line). fmt.yml runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` on every PR, so the formatting job fails. This also breaks AGENTS.md rule 3. Fix: split the chain the way rustfmt prints it.
findings.failureMode: The rustfmt CI job (fmt.yml: cargo fmt --all -- --check) fails on this PR.
findings.title: 101-char line fails `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (rule 3 / fmt CI)

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] messages, and lists hand-written Display/Error impls as its failure criterion. The new FileWriteError enum does exactly that (manual `impl std::fmt::Display` and `impl std::error::Error`), even though thiserror is already a tauri-bundler dependency and crate::Error uses it. Fix: `#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]` with `#[error("Failed to write file: {0}")] Write(#[source] io::Error)` and likewise for Permissions.
findings.failureMode: Violates mandatory repository rule 8 (thiserror for custom error types).
findings.title: FileWriteError hand-implements Display/Error instead of thiserror (AGENTS.md rule 8)

The shipped 10.0.0 package lists file version 10.0.25.52411 for all 141 assemblies, but this file lists 10.0.25.52413 (pre-RTM build). PackageOverrides.txt matches the package; this file does not. findings.description: The tearDown guard is `self.name.contains("testSelectBottomPlacement") || iPad()`. On iOS 17+ iPad, every OnboardingTests test now returns early, skipping `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Light")`, `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. The only test that needs the skip is testSelectBottomPlacement on iPad, which now calls XCTSkipIf before onboarding, so tearDown would otherwise run while the onboarding screen is up. testFirstRunTourDarkMode is not iPad-guarded and calls `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Dark")`. The app's DefaultThemeManager stores the theme in UserDefaults.standard, and ClearProfile's resetApplication() does not clear it; testFirstRunTourDarkMode itself relies on Dark surviving `app.terminate()`/`app.launch()`. So on iPad the Dark theme is never reset. The comment on line 30 ("the theme is not changed there") is only true for the skipped bottom-placement test. Fix: change `||` to `&&`.

The Dark theme stays in UserDefaults across ClearProfile relaunches, so later OnboardingTests tests and later test classes on that simulator run in Dark mode instead of Light.
findings.title: `|| iPad()` turns off the Light theme reset for every iPad test

findings.description: `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` was renamed to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`. XCTest only discovers methods whose names start with `test`, and nothing calls this method. FullFunctionalTestPlan does not list ShareLongPressTests in its skippedTests, so TestRail case 2864380 (share a bookmark to Reminders) quietly stops running there. AccessibilityTestPlan still names `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`, which now points at nothing. This also breaks AGENTS.md rule 6 (test methods start with `test`). Fix: restore the `test` prefix. To disable the test on purpose, use `throw XCTSkip` or a test-plan skip entry.

findings.description: The bookmark long-press went from `press(forDuration: 1.0)` to `pressWithRetry(duration: 0.5, …)`. BookmarksViewController uses a plain `UILongPressGestureRecognizer`, whose default minimumPressDuration is 0.5 s. A 0.5 s synthetic press therefore races the recognizer's timer. When the touch-up lands first, the press counts as a tap: `didSelectRowAt` calls `libraryPanelDelegate?.libraryPanel(didSelectURL:…)`, which opens the bookmark and dismisses the Library. pressWithRetry then retries on an element that no longer exists, so the retry can't recover. BookmarksTests long-presses the same cell with `pressWithRetry(duration: 1.5, …)`. Fix: use a duration safely above 0.5 s, such as 1.5 as in BookmarksTests.
findings.failureMode: testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteSendLinkDevice and testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteCopyURL fail intermittently: the 0.5 s press is sometimes taken as a tap, the bookmark opens instead of the context menu, and the retry or the `contextMenu.buttons["shareLarge"]` wait fails. This adds flakiness where the change meant to remove it.
findings.title: 0.5 s press sits exactly on the long-press threshold

findings.description: `tapIfExists` waits with `XCTWaiter().wait` on an `XCTNSPredicateExpectation`. That expectation evaluates its predicate once at the start and then about once per second. I checked this by running it on this host: a condition that became true after 0.05 s still timed out with a 0.5 s timeout, while a 1.5 s timeout completed at about 1.03 s. So `tapIfExists(timeout: 0.5)` is a single instant check made right after `pasteAction.waitAndTap()`. The pasteAction handler reads `UIPasteboard.general.string`, which triggers the system "Allow Paste" prompt. If that prompt appears even slightly after the check, it is never tapped. The alert then blocks the paste and `mozWaitForValueContains(urlBar, value: url)` times out. Fix: use a timeout above the ~1 s polling interval, such as 1.5 s.
findings.failureMode: In Copy-then-paste validations (for example testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteCopyURL and testHistoryShareNormalWebsiteCopyURL), an Allow Paste alert that appears after the single t=0 check is left on screen. The URL is never pasted and the test fails after the 20 s wait, so the flakiness this line was meant to fix remains.
findings.title: 0.5 s `tapIfExists` window only checks for the Allow Paste alert once

findings.description: The diff deletes `keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')...replace(r"\u", r"\\u")`. That code converted keywords into the `\uXXXX` form that `json.dumps` (ensure_ascii=True by default) writes into WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs, which are stored verbatim as TEXT/LONGTEXT. The new pattern `%你好%` never matches the stored `{"q": "\u4f60\u597d"}`, so a console or service-API log search for a CJK or Cyrillic term that appears in a run's inputs or outputs now returns no logs. The old pattern matched those runs (checked with a sqlite run). Fix: for the inputs/outputs conditions, escape the JSON-encoded form, e.g. `escape_like_pattern(json.dumps(keyword_trimmed)[1:-1])`, and keep the plain escaped value for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Console/service-API workflow log search with a non-ASCII keyword returns no logs even though matching runs exist.
findings.title: Non-ASCII workflow-log keyword search no longer matches JSON inputs/outputs

findings.description: escape_like_pattern() escapes with backslash (`50%` -> `50\%`), but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. IRIS then treats `\` as a literal and `%`/`_` as wildcards, so a fallback full-text query of "50%" becomes `%50\%%` and only matches text containing `50\`; "test_data" requires a literal backslash; a query with `\` requires two backslashes; a user `|` becomes an escape char. Base (`LIKE ?` without escaping) returned these rows. Fix: `ESCAPE '\'` (i.e. `ESCAPE '\\'` in the f-string) to match the helper.
findings.failureMode: IRIS full-text fallback (IRIS_TEXT_INDEX off) returns no documents for queries containing %, _ or \ that previously matched.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern is backslash-escaped

findings.description: The value is escaped with escape_like_pattern(), whose contract requires `ESCAPE '\'`. Unlike the parallel contains/start with/end with branches, this call is `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%")` with no `escape="\\"`. SQLAlchemy's MySQL dialect detects NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES and still renders the explicit `ESCAPE '\'` correctly for the sibling branches, but this branch compiles to a bare `NOT LIKE %s`. MySQL/OceanBase in that sql_mode then use no escape character, so "not contains 50%" (pattern `%50\%%`) only excludes text containing `50\`. Documents containing "50%" or "test_data" are wrongly kept, while "contains" on the same server works. Fix: `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%", escape="\\")`.
findings.failureMode: On a DB without a default backslash LIKE escape, "not contains" filters with %, _ or \ fail to exclude the matching documents.
findings.title: "not contains" metadata filter drops ESCAPE clause for escaped value

findings.description: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule 16 requires snake_case for Python variables and lists camelCase as a failure criterion. The new helper binds `escapedPattern = pattern.replace(...)`. Ruff ignores N806, so no linter catches it. Fix: rename to `escaped_pattern`, or return the expression directly.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory repository naming rule violated in new production code.
findings.title: camelCase local `escapedPattern` violates mandatory snake_case rule

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj) passes 7 objects but argc=6, so newobj is never read. Replication and AOF get `HSETEX h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1` with no value; the PR's own new test fails on exactly this stream. The replica rejects it ('wrong number of arguments for hsetex') and keeps the old value, and an AOF restart loses the increment. With propagation-error-behavior=panic* the replica or AOF load panics instead. Fix: pass argc 7.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT is replicated/AOF-logged as `HSETEX h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1` (missing value); replica errors and keeps stale value; AOF reload loses the increment (data loss / master-replica divergence).
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT propagation drops the value: argc 6 with 7 args

findings.description: The diff drops HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL (`HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` -> `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE`). Without that flag hashTypeSet persists an existing field (listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) / hfieldPersist). Reproduced: master HTTL f1 goes from 100 to -1 after HINCRBYFLOAT. This breaks the existing test 'HINCRBYFLOAT - preserve expiration time of the field', which expects HPTTL in 1..20. It also reverses the master/replica TTL divergence, because the replica applies KEEPTTL. HINCRBY still passes KEEP_TTL. Fix: restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1; HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1 -> master HTTL f1 returns -1 (TTL lost) while replica keeps ~100s TTL; field later expires on replica only.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now strips field TTL on master

findings.description: The diff removes `static` from addHashFieldToReply. All callers are in t_hash.c and no header declares it, so this violates AGENTS.md rule 7 (internal helpers must be static). nm on t_hash.o now shows the global symbol `T _addHashFieldToReply`. Fix: restore `static`.
findings.failureMode: An internal helper symbol is exported globally (mandate 7 violation), which pollutes the symbol namespace and can collide with module symbols.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply lost its static qualifier

findings.description: The diff deleted `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")`. WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs are LongText written with plain json.dumps (ensure_ascii=True), so "你好" is stored as `\u4f60\u597d`. The new pattern `%你好%` never matches that stored text, so searching logs with a CJK or other non-ASCII keyword returns nothing. Execution check: the base pattern matched and the head pattern did not. Fix: for the inputs/outputs conditions, apply unicode_escape to the keyword before escape_like_pattern, e.g. `escape_like_pattern(keyword_trimmed.encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8'))`.
findings.failureMode: Console and service-API workflow log search with a non-ASCII keyword returns zero logs even when run inputs/outputs contain it.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search loses non-ASCII (unicode_escape) matching

findings.description: escape_like_pattern() prefixes %, _ and \ with a backslash, but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. So the backslash is a literal character and the following %/_ stay wildcards. Query "50%" becomes `%50\%%`, which matches only text containing "50\". Execution check: '50% discount' and 'snake_case names' match 0 rows with ESCAPE '|' and 1 row with ESCAPE '\'. Any query containing %, _ or \ now returns nothing or the wrong rows. Fix: declare `ESCAPE '\'` so it matches the helper's escape character. Reached when IRIS_TEXT_INDEX=false, since the default is true.
findings.failureMode: IRIS full-text fallback (IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled) returns no or wrong documents for any query containing %, _ or \.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern escaped with backslash

findings.description: The value goes through escape_like_pattern, but `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%")` passes no `escape="\\"`, unlike the sibling contains/start with/end with branches. Compiled SQL: contains renders `LIKE ... ESCAPE '\\'`, while not contains renders a bare `NOT LIKE`. So this branch depends on the server's implicit LIKE escape. On MySQL/OceanBase/seekdb running with sql_mode NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES there is no implicit escape. Then "not contains 50%" treats `\` as a literal and `%` as a wildcard, fails to exclude documents whose metadata contains "50%", and stops being the complement of "contains", which still works via its explicit ESCAPE. The repo does not pin sql_mode. Fix: `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%", escape="\\")`.
findings.failureMode: Knowledge-retrieval metadata filter "not contains" returns wrong documents for values with %, _ or \ when the DB has no implicit backslash LIKE escape.
findings.title: "not contains" metadata filter omits escape="\\" after escaping value

findings.description: Repository mandate 16 (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) requires snake_case for Python variables. The new helper assigns and returns `escapedPattern`. Ruff's N806 is disabled in .ruff.toml, so no lint job catches it and the violation merges silently. Fix: rename it to `escaped_pattern`, or return the expression directly.
findings.failureMode: Violation of the mandatory naming rule in a new shared utility; not caught by CI because N806 is ignored.
findings.title: camelCase local `escapedPattern` violates mandatory snake_case rule

findings.description: Line 19 now requires '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link', but this PR doesn't rename services/lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js, which is still the only file in that directory at head. members.init() in boot runs require('./api'), which requires './members-api/members-api'. That require throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on any filesystem, since the names differ by a hyphen as well as by case. Fix: revert to '../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink', or rename the file too.
findings.failureMode: Ghost boot crashes in initServices() because members.init() throws "Cannot find module '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link'". The members API never loads, and so do the unit and e2e tests that load members-api.
findings.title: MagicLink require points to a file that doesn't exist

findings.description: Lines 12-13 now require '../email-service/email-event-storage' and '../email-service/email-event-processor'. This PR doesn't rename the email-service directory, which still holds EmailEventStorage.js and EmailEventProcessor.js. The base code required '../email-service/EmailEventStorage' and '../email-service/EmailEventProcessor'. EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() runs during boot and throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Fix: restore the PascalCase paths on both lines.
findings.failureMode: emailAnalytics.init() throws "Cannot find module '../email-service/email-event-storage'" inside initServices() Promise.all, so Ghost boot fails. Integration and e2e tests that call emailAnalytics.init() also fail.
findings.title: Email analytics requires email-service modules that were never renamed

findings.description: This hunk renames DonationBookshelfRepository.ts to donation-bookshelf-repository.ts. Its only importer, donation-service-wrapper.js, was renamed with no content change (+0 -0). It still runs require('./DonationBookshelfRepository') at line 11 inside init(), and no file by that name exists at head. donationService.init() therefore throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND during boot. Fix: change donation-service-wrapper.js line 11 to require('./donation-bookshelf-repository'). That file has no diff hunk, so this finding is anchored on the rename that causes the failure.
findings.failureMode: Ghost boot fails because donationService.init() in initServices() throws "Cannot find module './DonationBookshelfRepository'".
findings.title: Renaming DonationBookshelfRepository.ts breaks its unchanged importer

findings.description: The rewritten require statements on lines 1-4 and 6-10 lost their trailing semicolons. At base they were "const {Router} = require('express');" and so on. This breaks mandate #19, which requires explicit semicolons. It also breaks eslint-plugin-ghost's shared rule semi: ['error', 'always'], which lint:server applies to core/server/**/*.js. Nothing breaks at runtime, because each following line starts with const and ASI inserts the semicolons. Fix: restore the semicolons on lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
findings.failureMode: yarn lint (lint:server) reports 9 "Missing semicolon" semi errors in members-api.js and fails the lint/CI step.
findings.title: Semicolons dropped from the members-api.js require block

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC maps `.readerMode` to toggleReaderMode() and `.readerModeLongPressAction` to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which creates a reading-list record. Every showReaderMode dispatch (toolbar reader-mode tap, VoiceOver magic tap, summarizer long press) now saves the page to the reading list and shows a toast. Reader mode never turns on or off. No remaining code produces `.readerMode`. Fix: restore `displayView: .readerMode`.
findings.failureMode: User taps reader mode button on an article; instead of entering reader view, page is added to reading list and "Added to Reading List" toast shows; reader mode can never be toggled from the toolbar.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap now adds page to reading list instead of toggling reader mode

findings.description: Base: `url = (currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil`. Head: `url = (currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil`. Reader-mode URLs (http://localhost:PORT/reader-mode/page?url=...) are http, so base sent nil. The cancelEdit reducer (`toolbarAction.url ?? state.url`) then kept the decoded article URL that urlDidChange stored via `tab.url?.displayURL`. Head sends the raw internal localhost URL, which replaces the article URL in AddressBarState. The Tabs and Menu buttons call cancelEditMode even when not editing. Running the base and head expressions confirmed base returns nil and head keeps the localhost URL. Fix: restore `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: While viewing a page in reader mode, the user taps Tabs, Menu, or Cancel. The address bar URL becomes http://localhost:6571/reader-mode/page?url=… instead of the article's URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode condition inverted: reader-mode URL now kept

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry changed from `case .available: true` / `default: false` to `case .available: false` / `default: true`. That contradicts its own comment that `.available` means reader mode "will be enabled after action gets executed". Every reader-mode tap now reports the opposite enabled state. The existing test testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes also fails. Its default state has readerModeState nil, so head passes isEnabled=true. The existing extras mapping then records isPrivate=true, but the test asserts `savedExtras.isPrivate == false`. Fix: restore `.available: true`, `default: false`.
findings.failureMode: Tapping reader mode on an available page records the reader_mode_button_tapped event with the opposite enabled value; Glean data for open vs close is inverted.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled value inverted

findings.description: `private let gleanWrapper: GleanWrapper` became `let gleanWrapper: GleanWrapper`. This drops the explicit `private` modifier and exposes an implementation detail to the whole module. AGENTS.md rule 11 requires explicit access control, with `private` for implementation details. Nothing in the diff needs the wider access. Fix: restore `private let`.
findings.failureMode: Violates mandatory access-control rule 11; any module code can now call the wrapper directly and bypass ToolbarTelemetry's typed API.
findings.title: gleanWrapper access widened from private to implicit internal

findings.description: Flipping `"strict": true` to `"strict": false` in tsconfig.app.json breaks CI. `tsc -b --noEmit` now exits 2 with 242 TS errors; 47 of them are TanStack Router's `"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"`, the rest mostly ParamsReducerFn and zod-inference errors. With strict restored the same tree type-checks cleanly. That breaks the `npm run build` CI job (`tsc -b && vite build`) and `validate:types`. Type-aware ESLint also regresses: with strict off, `no-unsafe-assignment` errors appear on the `useWatch` lines in trigger-step (including the unchanged flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx), which pass with strict on, so `npm run lint` fails as well. The change also violates AGENTS.md rule 11, which requires strict mode. Fix: restore `"strict": true`.
findings.failureMode: Build and lint failures: `tsc -b` (used by the build and validate:types scripts) fails with 242 type errors, so the UI cannot be built, and type-aware ESLint starts reporting no-unsafe-assignment errors. Strict null and implicit-any checking, which rule 11 requires, is also lost.
findings.title: strict:false breaks tsc build and disables strict typing

findings.description: Only the work-pool Threshold handler uses global `parseInt(e.target.value)`; the deployment, work-queue, custom and flow-run-state handlers use `Number(...)`. (1) biome.json sets `style.useNumberNamespace` to "error", so `biome ci` (run by the UI v2 Checks Lint job) exits 1 with `lint/style/useNumberNamespace` at work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:78:42, the only error in the repo. (2) At runtime, clearing the field stores `NaN` in `trigger.threshold`. React logs "Received NaN for the `value` attribute" and zod reports "Expected number, received nan" rather than the min(1) message. Fix: use `Number(e.target.value)` as the sibling components do.
findings.failureMode: CI failure: `biome ci` fails on this line (useNumberNamespace is set to error). Clearing the input also stores NaN in form state, causing a React NaN warning and a confusing validation error.
findings.title: Work-pool threshold parseInt fails biome ci and stores NaN

findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` is stored unfiltered. `split` always returns at least one element, so the `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` branch can never produce undefined. A vitest probe confirmed that typing and then clearing the textarea leaves `trigger.expect` as `[""]`, and `form.trigger("trigger")` still validates. Typing `a` then Enter stores `["a",""]`. On the server, `expects()` treats an empty expect as "any event", but `matches("", event)` only matches an event named "", so this Reactive custom trigger would never fire. Fix: drop blank lines (`.filter((l) => l.trim() !== "")`) before the length check, so an empty textarea stores undefined, and keep the raw textarea text in local state so Enter still works.
findings.failureMode: Wrong form output: after typing and then clearing the events textarea, trigger.expect becomes [""] instead of undefined. The resulting automation matches no event rather than any event.
findings.title: Custom trigger stores blank lines; cleared textarea yields expect [""]

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields (line 36) and WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields (line 36) always bind the status to `trigger.expect`, including under Proactive ("Stays in"). A probe of Stays in + Paused produced `{posture:"Proactive",within:30,expect:["prefect.work-pool.paused"]}` with no `after`. Proactive triggers fire when expected events are absent (`meets_threshold`: Proactive and count < threshold), and with no `after` the buckets keep rolling. So this trigger fires on every 30s window without a paused event, whether or not the pool stayed paused. That is the opposite of "stays in Paused". The same diff's DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and the existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields ("Proactive: use after (states to stay in)") put the status in `after`, and the V1 UI maps Proactive status to after=[X] with expect=[other statuses]. Fix: bind the status to `trigger.after` for Proactive, with expect set to the other statuses.
findings.failureMode: Proactive ("Stays in") work pool and work queue status triggers get inverted semantics: they fire when the chosen status event is absent, not when the resource stays in that status.
findings.title: Work pool/queue "Stays in" status written to expect, inverting Proactive

findings.description: `<FormControl>` wraps the Radix `<Select>` root, which renders no DOM, so the generated form-item id never reaches the trigger. The "Status" FormLabel's `for` then points at a nonexistent element, and the `<SelectTrigger>` has no aria-label. A probe measured an accessible name of "" for the Status combobox in all three status components, and the label's target id does not exist. This affects deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:50, work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:47 and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:47. PostureSelect ("select posture") and the template select (id + htmlFor) are labelled. Fix: give each Status `<SelectTrigger>` an aria-label or an id matching the label.
findings.failureMode: Screen readers announce an unnamed combobox for Status, and getByLabelText("Status") cannot find the control.
findings.title: Status select has no accessible name

findings.description: After `navigator.performAction(Action.SelectLightTheme)` (which taps `lightThemeView`), the test now reads `app.buttons[...Appearance.darkThemeView].value` into `lightIsSelected` and asserts it equals "1". Base read `lightThemeView`. GenericImageOption sets `.accessibilityValue("\(isSelected ? 1 : 0)")`, so the dark option's value is "0" once light is selected. The assertion fails deterministically. DisplaySettingTests is not in FullFunctionalTestPlan's skippedTests, so that plan runs it. Fix: go back to `AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.lightThemeView`.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges always fails: XCTAssertEqual("0", "1") right after Light is selected, breaking the FullFunctionalTestPlan run.
findings.title: Light-theme check reads darkThemeView

findings.description: The diff moves `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` (deleted from before line 155) to after `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()`. At that point the UI is on the Shortcuts sub-page, which the test opened by tapping `Shortcuts.settingsPage` directly, so the navigator still thinks it is on HomeSettings. TopSitesSettingsViewController adds no rightBarButtonItem; only HomePageSettingViewController and AppSettingsTableViewController add a `.AppSettingsDone` button. So `app.buttons["Done"]` never appears and `waitAndTap` fails through XCTFail with continueAfterFailure=false. Base first ran the two navigator back actions (Shortcuts→Homepage→Settings) and only then tapped Done. The unchanged helper `validateNumberOfTopSitesDisplayed` uses the same goto-then-Done order. Even if Done were tapped, the goto that follows would try nav-bar back taps on the homepage. Fix: restore `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` before `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()`.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection times out looking for a Done button on the Shortcuts settings page and fails. FullFunctionalTestPlan does not skip it.
findings.title: Done tapped on Shortcuts page before navigating back

findings.description: The diff deletes `checkCopiedUrl()` (base line 71) right after `copyUrl()` in testClipboard. That helper runs only when `#unavailable(iOS 16.0)` and was the only check that `UIPasteboard.general.string` matches the URL bar. The remaining paste check is inside `if #available(iOS 17, *)`. On the iOS 15.0 deployment target, testClipboard now copies and opens a tab but asserts nothing about the clipboard. The PR only claims to delete testCopyLink and testSetCustomURLAsHome, and nothing visible replaces this check. `checkCopiedUrl` is now referenced only from commented-out code. Fix: restore the `checkCopiedUrl()` call after `copyUrl()`.
findings.failureMode: On an iOS 15 simulator, a regression where URL-bar Copy puts the wrong string (or nothing) on the pasteboard no longer fails testClipboard; the test passes vacuously.
findings.title: testClipboard lost its only iOS 15 clipboard assertion

findings.description: The diff changes `func checkUrl()` (line 11), `func copyUrl()` (line 17) and `func checkCopiedUrl()` (line 41) to `public func`. Grep shows checkUrl and copyUrl are called only from testClipboard in this file, and checkCopiedUrl is referenced only from a comment. ClipBoardTests itself is internal. AGENTS.md rule 11 lists 'marked public when they are only used internally' as a failure. The new public members also carry plain `//` comments rather than the `///` doc comments rule 14 requires for public API. Fix: drop the `public` modifier at all three sites. That restores the base declarations and clears both rules.
findings.failureMode: An AGENTS.md compliance check flags ClipBoardTests: three helpers used only inside the class are declared public (rule 11), and those public methods have no /// docs (rule 14). No build or runtime effect: swiftc -warnings-as-errors accepts it.
findings.title: Internal-only helpers newly marked public

findings.description: Loop bound changed from `j < keys_result->numkeys` to `j <= keys_result->numkeys`. The extra iteration reads keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] (past the numkeys*sizeof(int) allocation). For <6 keys, keysbuf[numkeys] is zeroed → pos 0 → argv[0] (command name) is hashed, so in cluster mode `SET foo bar`/`GET foo` return -CROSSSLOT (verified). For 6 same-slot keys, keys[6] aliases the `keys` pointer → garbage argv index → server crash (verified: `DEL {a}1..{a}6` → SIGBUS in extractSlotFromKeysResult via preprocessCommand). Also hits getSlotFromCommand (ASM feed/module propagate). Fix: restore `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Heap buffer overflow / OOB read → crash; mainline keyed commands in cluster mode rejected as CROSSSLOT; ASM migrations cancelled.
findings.title: Off-by-one `<=` in extractSlotFromKeysResult: CROSSSLOT on every keyed cmd, crash

findings.description: slot_buffer uses `malloc(...)` (line 1110) and `free(slot_buffer)` (lines 1120, 1124). server.h declares malloc/free `__attribute__((deprecated))` under __GNUC__ and src/Makefile WARN has `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`, so cluster.o fails to compile (verified: 3 errors) and redis-server cannot be built. Also violates AGENTS.md rules 2 (zmalloc/zfree only) and 4 (-Werror build). Fix: use zmalloc/zfree, or drop the unused slot_buffer entirely.
findings.failureMode: Build failure: `make` aborts on cluster.c with 'malloc'/'free' is deprecated errors; no server binary.
findings.title: malloc/free break the build (-Werror=deprecated-declarations); violate zmalloc rule

findings.description: `rendered = result.get("result")` is guarded only by `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)`, so None gets past the check and `return rendered` returns None from a method declared `-> str`. (1) CI's Python Style job runs basedpyright (strict) and mypy. Both fail on line 40: basedpyright reports `Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str"` and mypy reports `[return-value]`. (2) At runtime, an injected or subclassed executor (for example via the new DifyNodeFactory code_executor -> renderer wiring) whose result lacks `result` or has it set to None makes render_template return None. `_run` then evaluates `len(rendered)` and raises `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`, which escapes `except TemplateRenderError`. The node then fails as a generic WorkflowNodeError without inputs instead of a clean FAILED result. Fix: `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError("Template render result must be a string.")`.
findings.failureMode: An executor returns {} or {"result": None}, so render_template returns None and `len(None)` raises TypeError that escapes the TemplateRenderError handler. Separately, basedpyright and mypy fail the CI style job with a reportReturnType/return-value error on line 40.
findings.title: render_template can return None despite `-> str`; type checks fail and None crashes `len()`

findings.description: Every one of the 27 added tests (first at lines 451-457, `test_run_with_boolean_values`, through `test_run_with_escape_filter`) builds `TemplateTransformNode(..., graph=mock_graph, ...)`. The `__init__` this PR adds accepts only id, config, graph_init_params, graph_runtime_state and a keyword-only template_renderer, so each call raises `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'graph'`. The module also imports the nonexistent `core.workflow.graph_engine.entities.graph` and is named `*_spec.py`, which pytest does not collect ("no tests collected"). findings.description: escape_like_pattern() prefixes %, _ and \ with a backslash, but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. So the backslash is a literal character and the following %/_ stay wildcards. Query "50%" becomes `%50\%%`, which matches only text containing "50\". Execution check: '50% discount' and 'snake_case names' match 0 rows with ESCAPE '|' and 1 row with ESCAPE '\'. Any query containing %, _ or \ now returns nothing or the wrong rows. Fix: declare `ESCAPE '\'` so it matches the helper's escape character. findings.description: The value goes through escape_like_pattern, but `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%")` passes no `escape="\\"`, unlike the sibling contains/start with/end with branches. Compiled SQL: contains renders `LIKE ... ESCAPE '\\'`, while not contains renders a bare `NOT LIKE`. So this branch depends on the server's implicit LIKE escape. On MySQL/OceanBase/seekdb running with sql_mode NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES there is no implicit escape. Then "not contains 50%" treats `\` as a literal and `%` as a wildcard, fails to exclude documents whose metadata contains "50%", and stops being the complement of "contains", which still works via its explicit ESCAPE. The repo does not pin sql_mode. Fix: `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%", escape="\\")`.
findings.failureMode: Knowledge-retrieval metadata filter "not contains" returns wrong documents for values with %, _ or \ when the DB has no implicit backslash LIKE escape.
findings.title: "not contains" metadata filter omits escape="\\" after escaping value
